limitations: The runtime is unchanged; this is a tool and measurement checkpoint, not an adopted kernel speedup.
Scaling samples are three matched rounds per thread count after an outer warmup and per-process warmup. All samples retained; not a statistical parity certification.

Full-vector thread equality uses the pinned 215+32 history against the six-thread control; independent HF correctness here is the continuous excerpt NLL fixture. Earlier long HF gates remain separately documented.
No full-corpus, maximum-context, new architecture or independent 8B HF claim.
Instrumented projection timings include dispatch/wait in each operation; total wall time also includes instrumentation and is not mixed with benchmark timings.

Matrix probes use actual layer weights with fixed synthetic activations and cycle through all layer tensors for a case. They are kernel/dispatch diagnostics, not full inference or a numerical-accuracy gate against mx.
Reference matrix probes use the pinned ggml CPU graph API with a persistent threadpool and preallocated outputs/workspace. Reference Q8 activation conversion is part of the measured operation.
Displayed weight-byte rates are derived traffic estimates, not hardware DRAM counters.
Linux validation covers building and argument rejection in the measurement wrapper; existing runtime platform/HF gates were not redundantly rerun.
